pages.title: A drop of pond water
pages.html:
A drop of pond water

What if a single drop of water held more life than a whole city?

Maya squinted into the microscope. The drop she had scooped from the school pond was not empty at all. Tiny shapes spun, wriggled and raced across the glass.

Maya“They're alive, Omar. Every one of them.”

Omar“So what are they made of?”

In 1665 Robert Hooke asked the same question. Looking at cork, he saw little rooms and called them cells.

But what was hiding inside those rooms?

pages.title: The city in a cell
pages.html:
The city in a cell

Picture a busy city, shrunk a million times.

  • Cell membrane: the city wall, deciding what gets in and out.
  • Nucleus: city hall, holding the instruction book (DNA).
  • Cytoplasm: the streets, a jelly where everything moves.
  • Ribosomes: factories that build proteins.
Think about itIf the nucleus is city hall, what happens to a city that loses its plans?

pages.title: Power plants
pages.html:
Power plants

⚡

Every city needs power. In a cell, the power plants are the mitochondria.

glucose + oxygen → energy + CO₂ + water

Your muscle cells are packed with mitochondria, because running and jumping need lots of energy.

Try it

Do 20 jumping jacks. Why are you breathing faster? Where is that oxygen going?

pages.title: Plant or animal?
pages.html:
Plant or animal?

Omar held up a leaf. “Same city?” Maya grinned. “Same city, extra buildings.”

Plant cells also havea stiff cell wall, a big vacuole for water, and chloroplasts to make food from sunlight.
Spot the differenceAnimal cells are rounder and flexible; plant cells look like neat green bricks.

Ready to prove you can tell them apart?

quiz.explanation: Hooke saw little rooms in cork in 1665 and called them cells.

quiz.q: Which part holds the cell's DNA?
quiz.explanation: The nucleus is the control centre and stores DNA.
Mitochondria release energy during cellular respiration.

quiz.q: Which is found in plant cells but not animal cells?
Why do muscle cells have many mitochondria?
quiz.explanation: Movement uses a lot of energy, so muscles need many power plants.
